answer: Admission is priced by a memory-hard proof re-checked against a rotating seed. Each applicant derives a 1 GB table from the epoch seed, keeps it resident, and answers 64 random probes within two seconds; the node records the table digest as the identity relic. Since the seed rotates every epoch, a precomputed table is worthless next round and cannot be carried forward. An attacker running N agents must keep N distinct tables warm, so 1,000 identities need a terabyte of live RAM rather than one key duplicated. Cold-disk probes miss the ledge and are rejected without an echo to the grader.
